html:
The Battle of Beth Horon was fought in November 66 CE at the pass of Beth Horon, northwest of Jerusalem in today's West Bank. Jewish rebels ambushed a Roman army as it retreated and beat it badly.

The First Jewish-Roman War had begun that summer, when the people of Judea rose against Roman rule and wiped out the garrison in Jerusalem. Cestius Gallus, the governor of Syria, marched south with the Twelfth Legion and many other troops, about 30,000 men in all. He reached Jerusalem and attacked the Temple area, then gave up and turned back, for reasons that are still not clear. In the narrow pass of Beth Horon the rebels attacked his column from the heights. The Romans lost about 6,000 men, their baggage and siege engines, and the legion's eagle.

It was one of the worst defeats Rome ever suffered in a rebel province. It convinced many Jews that the revolt could win, and a rebel government was set up in Jerusalem. The emperor Nero sent Vespasian with a much larger army. Four years later his son Titus destroyed Jerusalem and the Temple. The only detailed source is Josephus.
sum: The Battle of Beth Horon was fought in November 66 CE at the pass of Beth Horon, northwest of Jerusalem in today's West Bank. Jewish rebels ambushed a Roman army as it retreated and beat it badly.
